newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Alatas urges trade unity among developing states.
newsitem.headline: Alatas urges trade unity among developing states.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas urged developing nations on Tuesday to unite in a battle against global economic inequity and to ensure the success of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
"Developing countries as a whole remain marginalised from the international economic decision-making process," Alatas said.

He accused "certain developed countries" of seeking to impose a new form of protectionism by proposing to link such issues as labour and environmental standards to the WTO trade talks to be held in Singapore in December.
Alatas was giving the opening address at a two-day seminar organised by the ambassadors of nine Latin American and Caribbean states to boost trade and other ties with Indonesia.
"All developing countries...are called upon to make a common stand and prevent the weakening of the WTO at this fragile stage of its infancy," the minister said.

The developing nations of Southeast Asia oppose demands by the United States and some other developed powers to include such items as labour standards and environmental issues on the WTO's December agenda.

Alatas said developing countries should work together to protect their rights. "Success in South-South cooperation will also demonstrate developing countries can contribute significantly to global economic development," he added.

He noted that two-way trade between Indonesia and the Latin American and Caribbean states was just over US$1 billion in 1994 and $1.56 billion last year, with an Indonesian deficit of $350 million and $566 million, respectively.
"Naturally, we should like to substantially reduce that deficit even as we increase total trade volume," Alatas said.
He said the two sides should take concrete steps in gathering and sharing information and also in boosting the involvement of the private sector.
The countries participating in the seminar are Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, Mexico, Panama, Peru and Venezuela.
